title: Sell Mineral Rights in Homewood, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Homewood, AL | Offer
metaDescription: Homewood, Jefferson County mineral owner with an inherited interest tied to older family land? Get an honest cash offer, no pressure to sell.
heroLead: Homewood is one of the older, more established suburbs just south of downtown Birmingham, and the mineral interests tied to families here often go back further than the neighborhood itself.
intro: We occasionally hear from a Homewood homeowner who is surprised to learn they hold a mineral interest at all, usually because it came down through a grandparent's estate connected to land somewhere else in the county, not necessarily under their current house. If that is your situation, we can help you sort out exactly what you own and where.

sections.heading: Inherited interests versus interests under your home
paragraphs: Most of the time, a Homewood resident's mineral interest is not actually located under their own lot. Homewood itself was largely developed and platted decades ago, so any mineral rights that exist locally were usually severed long before the current homes were built. What we more often see is a Homewood family holding an interest in western or northern Jefferson County land inherited from an earlier generation.
That distinction matters because it means selling your mineral interest has nothing to do with your home's deed or mortgage. It is a separate asset entirely, wherever the actual acreage sits.

sections.heading: Getting a fair number without the runaround
paragraphs: We ask for the legal description, a recent royalty statement if you have one, and any probate paperwork tied to how you received the interest. From there we can usually turn around a quote within a few business days, explained in plain terms rather than a spreadsheet you have to decode yourself.

faqs.question: I live in Homewood but the mineral interest is in another county listed on my deed. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes, we evaluate the interest based on where the acreage actually sits, not where you personally live, so a Walker or Tuscaloosa County tract is no problem.

faqs.question: Will selling affect my property taxes on my Homewood house?
faqs.answer: No, mineral rights are taxed and assessed separately from your residential property, so a sale has no bearing on your homestead.

faqs.question: How do I find out what county my inherited interest is actually in?
faqs.answer: The legal description on your deed or division order will list the county, section, township, and range, and we can help you interpret it if it is unclear.

faqs.question: Is there a cost to getting a quote?
faqs.answer: No, evaluating your interest and giving you a number costs you nothing, and you decide from there whether to move forward.
